about: Belief questions used by Vote Helper. Part 1 (general) carries across elections. Part 2 (specific) is asked only when a ballot item doesn't map cleanly onto general beliefs. Answers are never stored here; they live in each person's browser or private beliefs file.

scale.position: -2 = strongly agree with side A, 0 = in between or no view, +2 = strongly agree with side B
scale.importance: 0 = doesn't matter to me, 1 = a little, 2 = matters (default), 3 = one of my top issues

general.label: Taxes and public services
general.q: When the state or your city wants more money for services, where do you lean?
general.a: Pay more in taxes to fund more or better services
general.b: Keep taxes and spending lower, even if services shrink

general.label: Taxing high earners and the very wealthy
general.q: How should California treat its highest earners and wealthiest residents?
general.a: They should pay a larger share, including new or higher taxes
general.b: Don't single them out; high taxes on them drive people and jobs away

general.label: State borrowing (bonds)
general.q: How do you feel about the state borrowing money through bonds?
general.a: Borrowing is fine for long-term investments like housing or research
general.b: Avoid new debt; pay as we go or don't do it

general.label: Saving for downturns
general.q: When the state has extra money in good years, what should it do?
general.a: Spend it on current needs and programs
general.b: Put more into reserves for recessions

general.label: Vote needed to pass taxes
general.q: What share of voters should it take to pass a local special tax?
general.a: A simple majority should be enough
general.b: Taxes should need a two-thirds supermajority

general.label: Voter power vs. elected officials
general.q: How much should voters decide directly (initiatives, recalls) versus elected officials?
general.b: Rely more on elected officials and set processes

general.label: Housing growth
general.q: How should California and San Luis Obispo handle housing?
general.a: Protect neighborhood scale and local control, even if fewer homes get built
general.b: Build much more housing, faster, including denser buildings

general.label: Environmental review vs. speed
general.q: When big projects (housing, water, energy, transit) are proposed, what matters more?
general.a: Thorough environmental review and the public's right to challenge it
general.b: Faster, cheaper approvals, even with less review

general.label: Climate and energy
general.q: What should come first in energy policy?
general.a: Aggressive climate action: cut emissions, no new offshore oil
general.b: Lower gas and power bills first; fewer climate mandates

general.label: Voting rules
general.q: How should California balance easy voting and verification?
general.a: Make voting as easy as possible, including mail ballots for everyone
general.b: Require ID and stricter verification, even if it adds steps

general.label: Money in campaigns
general.q: Should public money ever go to candidates' campaigns?
general.a: Yes, public financing can reduce big-donor influence
general.b: No, taxpayer money shouldn't fund campaigns

general.label: Government oversight of organizations
general.q: How much should government regulate how businesses, insurers and nonprofits operate?
general.a: Lighter rules; let organizations decide how to run themselves
general.b: Stronger rules and oversight to protect the public

general.label: Crime and justice
general.q: What's the better approach to public safety?

general.label: Gender identity and parental notification in schools
general.q: On school policies about gender identity, where do you lean?
general.a: Protect students' privacy and current state LGBTQ+ protections
general.b: Notify parents; restrict girls' sports to students born female

general.label: School choice
general.q: How should California approach charter schools and school choice?

general.label: California and the federal government
general.q: How should California's state officials deal with the current federal administration?
general.a: Challenge federal policies in court when they hurt California

general.label: Party lean
general.q: In partisan races, which party's approach do you generally prefer? (Pick the middle if you don't lean.)

general.label: Experience vs. fresh faces
general.q: All else equal, who do you prefer in office?

specific.q: If voters recall a governor, how should the replacement be chosen?

options.l: Voters pick a replacement on the same ballot (current system)
The lieutenant governor serves, or a later election fills the seat (Prop 5's approach)

specific.q: Prop 38 would send half of an $8.4B research bond to one institute chosen by the measure's criteria. Is that OK with you?

options.l: Fine, if the research is good
No, all of it should be open to competitive grants

specific.q: Prop 40 is a one-time 5% tax on billionaires' total net worth (assets, not income). How do you feel about taxing wealth this way?

options.l: I'd rather tax income, not wealth

specific.q: Should the state require nonprofit community clinics to spend at least 90% of their revenue on care, with penalties if they don't?

options.l: No, let clinics decide how to spend

specific.q: Should the elected Board of Equalization be phased out and its remaining duties moved to other state tax agencies?
Should California create a public disaster (home) insurance program instead of relying mainly on private insurers?
Judges on retention ballots run unopposed and can't campaign. When no problem with a judge has been found, what's your default?
